_comment: Functional state of the physical GPIB bus, captured read-only through a
real Prologix GPIB-ETHERNET adapter (firmware 01.06.06.00).
Every 'measured' value below is a verbatim instrument reply with its
terminator shown explicitly. Values marked 'derived' follow the same
documented construction but were not observed directly -- they are marked
so nobody mistakes an inference for a measurement.
Regenerate with: python tools/ab_instruments.py --host <adapter>

bus_wide_findings.terminator: LF (0x0A) on every instrument; no CR anywhere

integer_signing.note: *ESR? reads '+36' on a 34411A and '116' on a Keithley

serial_poll_idle.note: MAV (0x10) sets on top. Bit 2 tracks the error queue on the Agilent/HP units, so a unit idling at 0 reads 4 once its queue is dirty.

bus_wide_findings.unit_query: A bare UNIT? is silent on every DMM tested

_comment: Deliberately NOT recorded as per-instrument measurements. The queue
contents observed during profiling were dominated by errors the
profiling itself caused, so they describe our tooling, not the
instruments. What IS durable is the mechanism below.
An ungated '++read' costs two error-queue slots on any query the
instrument does not implement: -113 'Undefined header' for the query,
then -420 'Query UNTERMINATED' because the read addressed a device
with nothing to say. A full probe battery overflowed the queues on
four of the seven instruments here (-350 'Queue overflow'), which
destroys whatever real errors were in them.
Discarding a socket buffer without consuming the instrument's reply
leaves it addressed to talk, and the next query then logs -410
'Query INTERRUPTED'.
tools/buslib.py now gates every read on the MAV bit for this reason.
Anything reading this bus should do the same.
emulator_behaviour: IMPLEMENTED. The emulator keeps a per-instrument FIFO and latches the
matching *ESR? bits. SYST:ERR? drains one entry per query, *CLS and
Three codes are raised, using the SCPI-99 standard text: -113 on a
query for a node the instrument does not have, -410 when a query
arrives over an unread reply, and -420 when a read finds nothing
queued. The last two are raised by the gateway, which is where the
and per-model queue depths. Those are instrument bookkeeping. The
queue here exists to tell a developer what their client did, and both
of those codes were also the only ones whose text varied by vendor.
An unrecognised SET command does not raise -113. It is indistinguish-
able from a valid one the emulator accepts silently, so raising there
would invent failures; under-reporting is the safer error.

1.name: Keithley 2002
notes: CONF? equals FUNC? -- no range/resolution pair, unlike Agilent.
Reading carries elements: value, timestamp, reading number, channel.
Mantissa is NOT normalised: 10 V reads +10.000086E+00, exponent E+00.
Only the 10 V DC case is measured; the fixed E+00 exponent is derived.

2.name: Keithley 2001M
notes: Same element format as the 2002 but five decimals, not six.

3.name: Keithley 2010
notes: Does NOT use the element format its 2001/2002 siblings do.
Plain normalised scientific, eight decimals.

4.name: Fluke PM6690
notes: Identity uses ', ' separators -- every other instrument uses bare ','.
Readings express a fixed RESOLUTION (0.01 Hz), not a fixed digit count:
+9.99999962E+06 has eight decimals, +1.000000038E+07 has nine, and both
are the same measurement one second apart. Digit count moves with the
decade, so it is NOT a READ?-versus-FETC? distinction.

5.name: Agilent 34411A

_comment: Both blocks are measured. This instrument gets reconfigured at the
bench, so neither is 'the' state -- the DC-volts block was captured
with a 10 V reference on the inputs, this one with a 10k thermistor.
As of the last check it was back in TEMP.
Note READ? in TEMP mode with the voltage reference still connected
returns -9.90000000E+37, SCPI's not-a-number marker.

notes: DC-volts CONF? is VERIFIED and the emulator already matched it byte
for byte -- the eight-decimal range/resolution pair inferred from the
temperature capture was correct.
This unit is reconfigured at the bench between sessions, so check its
actual mode before treating either block as current.
CONF? parameters carry EIGHT decimals; our earlier six were wrong.
VOLT:DC:AVER:STAT? and AVER:COUN? are silent -- no such nodes.
RANG? reports the range in USE under autoranging (10 V here, 0.1 V
on the thermistor), so it tracks the signal, not a fixed maximum.

6.name: Agilent 33250A
notes: FUNC? returns a BARE waveform name with no quotes -- unlike every
measuring instrument on this bus, which quotes its function.
Serial poll idles at 0, not 4.
Output was OFF throughout; no active-mode behaviour was exercised.

7.name: HP E3631A
notes: NO TestController driver exists -- AgilentHP E363xA.TXT covers the
E3632A/E3633A/E3634A only. Kept out of the startup bench for that
reason; a name that resolves to no driver breaks the client's load.
APPL? is QUOTED, unlike every other reply this unit gives.
MEAS:VOLT? is the meter, not the setpoint: -0.481 V with output off
while VOLT? reads +0.000.
*OPT? and the VOLT:PROT subsystem genuinely do not exist on this model.
Serial poll idles at 0 and reads 16 with data pending, not 20.
Read-only throughout: this supply may be connected to a load.
